newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy industry ministry sees CPI at 2.5 pct in 97.
newsitem.headline: Italy industry ministry sees CPI at 2.5 pct in 97.

text.p: Latest consumer price data suggests it will be possible for Italy to meet the government's target of average annual inflation of 2.5 percent in 1997, the Industry Ministry said on Thursday.

The ministry, which oversees a price watch committee, was commenting in a statement on figures from the statistics institute ISTAT which showed consumer prices rose 3.4 percent year-on-year in August, down from 3.6 percent in July.
The year-on-year figure, in line with provisional data from sample cities late last month, was the lowest since 1969 and the seventh successive monthly fall.
"The ministry notes with satisfaction that the consumer price index in August has been confirmed at 3.4 percent," the statement said.
"This figure suggests that it will be possible to attain the ceiling of 2.5 percent set (by the government) for 1997," it said.

A previous 1997 target of 3.0 percent was lowered to 2.5 percent by the new centre-left government of Prime Minister Romano Prodi which took office last May in its three-year plan of economic and financial objectives for 1997-99.
